scenes.narration: The Moon has ice. That part is settled. What nobody can say for sure is whose water it is.

scenes.narration: Five suspects are on the table. Comets. Asteroids. The Moon's own volcanoes. The solar wind. And, strangest of all, our own planet.
scenes.visual_brief: A comet streaming its tail across space, hinting at a lineup of suspects.

scenes.overlay_hint: Five small hairline markers appear one by one

scenes.narration: One measurement could go a long way toward settling the case, and nobody has made it yet. We will get to it.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 low flight over cratered lunar south pole terrain with long shadows, teal tint, amber sunlight sliver, no text

scenes.narration: And we will look at a lander built to attempt it, which missed its launch window this year. First, the scene of the crime.

scenes.overlay_hint: Small label: Illustration if AI is used

scenes.overlay_hint: Big number: about 5 percent water by mass, with a range bracket

scenes.narration: Why was there ice in there at all? The Moon barely tilts on its axis. So the floors of some polar craters never see the Sun.
scenes.visual_brief: Sunlight sweeping over polar terrain while crater floors stay in shadow.
scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 low sun raking across polar lunar crater rims, floors in deep black shadow, teal and amber contrast, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Thin axis line showing a tilt of about one and a half degrees only if sourced

scenes.narration: Many of these shadows are cold enough to trap ice, at about one hundred and ten kelvin or colder.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 deep permanently shadowed lunar crater interior lit only by faint reflected light, frost-blue tones, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Temperature scale marker at 110 kelvin

scenes.narration: That is minus one hundred and sixty three degrees Celsius. They are called cold traps.

scenes.overlay_hint: Thermometer scale: minus 163 Celsius highlighted in amber

scenes.narration: One estimate puts them at about forty thousand square kilometres. That is a bit less than Switzerland.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 polar view of the Moon with shadowed patches glowing teal against grey terrain, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Area comparison: about 40,000 square kilometres vs Switzerland

scenes.narration: So the ice is real. The question is how it got there. Suspect one. Comets.

scenes.overlay_hint: Lower third: SUSPECT ONE - COMETS

scenes.narration: A comet is a dirty snowball. It looks like the obvious answer. And in 2022, a team analysed the chemical fingerprint of the LCROSS plume.
scenes.visual_brief: Close view of a real comet nucleus, rough and dusty.
scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 dark rocky comet nucleus with jets of gas and dust, sunlit, no text

scenes.narration: They compared it with volcanoes, and with asteroid-like material. Neither matched well. Comets did.
scenes.visual_brief: The LCROSS Centaur impact flash at Cabeus.
scenes.ai_prompt: Illustration, cinematic 16:9 three labelled-free spectral lines in teal and amber over a dark lunar crater, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Three hairline bars: volcano, asteroid, comet; comet highlighted amber

scenes.narration: That sounds like a case closed. But it is not. A 2025 review of lunar ice theories sees it differently.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 icy comet racing through colourful nebula backdrop, streaks of light, no text

scenes.narration: Comets hit the Moon very fast, and a fast impact keeps less water. So the review treats comets as a minor source.

scenes.narration: Remember that disagreement. These are two serious lines of evidence pointing different ways.

scenes.narration: One is a chemical fingerprint from a single impact at a single crater. The other is impact physics applied to the whole Moon.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 oblique view of a lunar polar crater with a single highlighted ring, dark ground, no text

scenes.narration: And Cabeus may not speak for every cold trap. Suspect two. Asteroids.

scenes.narration: That is why the review leans on them, while the fingerprint study found asteroid-like material a poor match. Same suspect, two verdicts.

scenes.narration: Suspect three. The Moon itself. Volcanism on the Moon peaked early, roughly four to two billion years ago.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 vast dark lunar basalt plains with sinuous rilles, golden light, no text

scenes.narration: Eruptions vented gas, and some of it was water. The review calls outgassing and impacts the largest sources of polar ice.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 volcanic plume rising over a glowing alien landscape, amber and teal, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Small label: Illustration if AI is used

scenes.narration: How much would it take? According to a NASA slide deck, if only about one tenth of one percent of the water

scenes.narration: vented in the big eruptions was trapped in shadow, that could account for today's ice.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 gas wisps settling into a deep shadowed crater and freezing, teal frost, no text

scenes.narration: That is an estimate, not a measurement. But it shows the idea does not need a miracle.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 Cosmic Cliffs nebula in gold and blue, drifting stars, no text

scenes.narration: There is another reason this matters. The old story said the giant impact that made the Moon left it bone dry.

scenes.ai_prompt: Illustration, cinematic 16:9 Earth-sized collision with glowing debris disc coalescing into the Moon, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Small label: Illustration

scenes.visual_brief: Apollo 17 orange volcanic soil.
scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 macro shot of tiny orange and black volcanic glass beads, no text

scenes.narration: So the Moon may have had water of its own to give. Suspect four. The Sun.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 burning Sun with solar prominence arcing, amber and orange, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Lower third: SUSPECT FOUR - THE SUN

scenes.narration: The solar wind is a constant stream of protons. At the Moon, about two trillion hit each square metre every second.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 streams of glowing particles flowing from the Sun toward a small grey Moon, teal and amber, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Counter: about 2 trillion per square metre per second

scenes.narration: When protons strike dusty soil, they can make hydroxyl and water in the grains.
scenes.visual_brief: Close-up of fine lunar dust and soil.
scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 macro of grey lunar dust grains with faint teal sparks, no text

scenes.narration: China's Chang'e-5 brought back samples that show it. The grains hold roughly eleven hundred to twenty five hundred parts per million hydrogen.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 sealed container of dark lunar soil under laboratory light, hairline teal frame, no text
scenes.overlay_hint: Range bracket 1100 to 2500 ppm hydrogen

scenes.narration: The signature points strongly to the solar wind. So the Sun waters the Moon's skin.

scenes.narration: But does it fill the polar traps? The review says probably not.

scenes.narration: That sounds slow, but over billions of years it adds up. The real objection is temperature.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 Pillars of Creation in gold and teal, drifting stars, no text

scenes.narration: Making molecular water needs about four hundred kelvin. The cold traps are far colder.

scenes.ai_prompt: Cinematic 16:9 thermal map of the Moon with glowing amber hot zone and blue cold poles, no text

scenes.narration: Hydrogen from the wind might still migrate to the poles. That is debated.

scenes.narration: I want to be careful here. That is a ceiling, not a forecast. The mainstream view still favours other sources.

director_notes: Bolum bir sorusturma dosyasi gibi kurgulandi: bes saniginin her biri (kuyruklu yildiz, asteroit, Ay volkanlari, Gunes ruzgari, Dunya) kendi gorsel dunyasina sahip, ve her gecis 'Suspect' alt baslik cizgisiyle isaretleniyor. Kanit anlari (LCROSS, Chang'e-5, Kaguya, ShadowCam, 2026 calismasi) gercek NASA fotograflari ve ince cizgi grafikleri ile verilir. Genel cumleler renkli, hareketli kozmik ara planlarla (nebula, galaksi, Gunes, aurora) beslenir. Her sahne hareketli, yaklasik yarisi video; ayni gorsel iki kez kullanilmaz. Chang'e-7 icin sahte bir benzeri kullanilmaz, gerekirse 'Illustration' etiketi ile cizim kullanilir.
